title: Japanese Asset Bubble: 1989
description: A quick win: understand Japanese Asset Bubble: 1989.

hook.text: In 1989, Tokyo's Imperial Palace grounds were worth more than all of California's real estate. Then it burst.

buildup.text: Japan's Nikkei index rose from 10,000 in 1984 to nearly 39,000 in 1989, fueled by cheap credit and speculation.

discovery.text: When the Bank of Japan raised rates to cool speculation, stocks and real estate began a multi-decade decline.

twist.text: The Nikkei didn't recover its 1989 peak until 2024—thirty-five years later. Japan's 'lost decades' became a warning.

climax.text: Japan proved that markets don't always recover quickly. Sometimes the pain lasts a generation.

punchline.text: Not every crash bounces back quickly. Some take decades.

quiz.question: How long did it take Japan's Nikkei to recover its 1989 peak?
